title: Quick gut + mechanics note — Caleb Navarro on runtime loop
content:
Short personal scratchpad after the loop (raw, non-polished). Purpose: capture first impressions, measurable mechanics, and candidate follow-ups while fresh.

Context:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving)
- Interviewers: Maya (system-design), Rafaela (coding), me for take-home/onsite coordination
- Time: 60m coding + 45m design + 15m culture Qs

Quick verdict (gut): leaning positive but with caveats. Candidate shows strong systems intuition; shaky on edge-case correctness and some API ergonomics. Could be senior with short ramp, but may need pairing on production hardening.

Coding probe notes (concrete):
- Prompt: implement an in-memory prefix-KV cache with eviction by LRU and simple TTL semantics.
- What they did: picked LRU + doubly-linked list + hashmap, explained complexity clearly. Implemented core ops (get/set/delete) and TTL check on access.
- Strengths: clear time/space reasoning, tested common paths manually, explained tradeoffs for sharding later.
- Gaps/bugs: TTL removal only on access (lazy) — acceptable but didn't mention memory-growth risk for cold keys; eviction logic had off-by-one in list re-link when re-inserting head after hit (I reproduced locally during whiteboard).
- Follow-up ask: ask for small unit tests or a short patch to fix re-link bug and add background sweep (15–30m follow-up).

System-design notes (measurable):
- Scenario: autoscaling inference pool with KV cache affinity and cross-model cache reuse.
- Candidate approach: strong—proposed routing layer that hashes by client-session for KV locality, suggested per-model namespaces and small shared hot-key cache for embeddings.
- Took latency SLOs seriously (p50/p95 targets) and prioritized single-tenant fallback plan during scale spikes.
- Missed items: didn’t fully address cold-start cost across many model variants (could ask them to sketch a cheap eviction/prefetch policy).

Behavioral/culture bits:
- Communication: concise, asks clarifying Qs early, pauses to confirm assumptions.
- Collaboration: emphasized shipping with docs and on-call runbooks; volunteered to pair on rollout playbooks in past role.
- Questions they asked: about postmortem culture, SLAs, ownership model (good signal).

Red flags / risks:
- Edge-case correctness in low-level code (possible source of production incidents if unchecked).
- Limited exposure to very large multi-tenant fleets (has experience up to ~200 GPUs but not 1000+).

Actionable next steps (my proposal):
1) Request small overwrite patch: fix re-link bug + add 3 tiny unit tests + note about TTL background sweep (estimate: 45m). If they complete, move to hire conversation.
2) If no patch, schedule a follow-up 30m design drill focused on cold-start mitigation and prefetch heuristics.
3) Reference check (ops manager at last company) focusing on incident triage and low-level debugging.

Suggested hire recommendation (for hiring committee):
- Recommend: hire with strong engineering laddering (Senior I level) contingent on the small patch OR a clean design follow-up.
- Compensation expectation: candidate hinted at 170–200k base range (US-West), negotiable for equity.

Notes to self (random):
- Save link to their GitHub — check for prior infra libs and tests style.
- If we push to take-home, give explicit rubric: correctness (40%), performance (30%), tests & docs (30%).

Unresolved questions I want to capture before panel sync:
- Exact timeline for their current notice period (they said 4 weeks but might be flexible).
- Any gaps in multi-tenant scaling at >500 GPU scale—ask about design choices there.

End of raw scratchpad. Will tidy if we move to formal scorecard.
